subject: physical-education
title: Synthesis and review: progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment under transfer
focus: progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment
essentialQuestion: How do I make a movement better before I make it heavier or faster?
privacySafeScenario: Build a technique-first strength and mobility progression, document the criteria for advancing each movement, and show a completed progression with the criteria met.
studentTask: Learner works progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment programmed into the learner’s live plan and progressed across sessions, including one hold or regression made deliberately at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment programmed into the learner’s live plan and progressed across sessions, including one hold or regression made deliberately, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
